what: Object system identification (mass, yaw inertia, friction) on the full dynamics of a floating-base humanoid, by adjoint Gauss-Newton through the exact-cone contact step, against the Cramer-Rao bound computed from the same Fisher matrix.
setup: 512 envs, 100 steps, the robot's M, nle and J recomputed at the integrated state every step; 5 contacts, 15 virtual rows; NCP natural residual max 4.213074e-12 over 512 x 100 steps

same_model_both_sides.note: generator and estimator are one model, not two; the residual at the true parameters is the floor

on_the_cramer_rao_bound.note: the median of a zero-mean normal error of scale CRB is 0.6745 CRB; the measurement sits on it, so the error is information-bound, not a local minimum

acceptance.gate: p95 < 0.05 for m and mu at sigma_tau = 1 N m over 50 steps
acceptance.reason: the CRB itself is 5.726e-02 per N m at that window, so the gate is below the bound

truth_start_control.conclusion: Gauss-Newton is not stuck in local minima

fisher_roc.note: the oracle is below 0.8 at 50 steps, so an AUC of 0.9 is unreachable with this observable, not with this estimator

baselines_median_m_error.note: the recursive estimator beats Gauss-Newton on mu alone when it is handed the true mass

known_defects: coplanar corner contacts give condition number 3e17; the fix is an epsilon = 0.02 compliance as virtual degrees of freedom
the first estimator has errors in variables and needs the total-least-squares form
earlier attempts that froze M, Minv, nle and J over the trajectory were rejected: the result was an artefact of the frozen stance
